memory_leads.lead: A port agent acts on behalf of an identified principal for a bounded port call or service scope; the principal may be an owner/operator, charterer or another party depending on appointment. Agency role should remain separate from vessel ownership, charter control and terminal operation.

A nominated agent, formally appointed agent, protective agent and husbandry-focused service role can represent different interests or scopes during the same call. Nomination alone should not be treated as proof of the final agency mandate or liability allocation.

Port-call execution begins before arrival through appointment, voyage/ETA updates, port information exchange and pre-arrival document or data preparation. The information-ready state can therefore lead or lag the vessel's physical approach to port.

A pro-forma disbursement estimate and advance/funding request form a distinct cash-planning state before the call, while actual invoices and final disbursement reconciliation occur later. Estimated port cost, funded cash and final cost should not be collapsed into one number.

Berth prospects, terminal readiness, cargo sequence and service availability are coordinated across the vessel, agent, terminal/stevedore and port-side providers. The agent can coordinate these dependencies without controlling the terminal's physical capacity or the charterparty rights triggered by delay.

Pilotage is a distinct navigational service/interface in port approach, shifting and departure. Pilot ordered, available, embarked and completed are operational states separate from berth availability and from the master's continuing command responsibilities.

Towage and mooring/unmooring services are separate port-call resources whose ordering, readiness and completion can constrain arrival, shifting or departure even when berth and cargo operations are otherwise ready.

Customs, immigration, port-health and other authority interfaces create documentary or clearance states distinct from terminal cargo readiness. A vessel can be physically alongside yet still face unresolved entry, crew, cargo or departure formalities.

Husbandry can include crew transport/change support, provisions, spares delivery, medical or welfare arrangements and other vessel-support services. Service requested, locally arranged, delivered and receipted are distinct from the seafarer's underlying employment or immigration status.

Port agents often coordinate independent surveyors, class/insurer-related attendance, technicians and other specialists when required. Coordination of attendance is not the same as the surveyor's independent finding, class decision, insurer position or technical acceptance.

Port-call event records such as arrival, anchoring, pilot, all-fast, NOR-related communications, cargo-operation milestones and sailing times can feed statement-of-facts or post-fixture documentation. Event recording, contractual interpretation and eventual laytime claim are separate layers.

Departure readiness is a conjunction of cargo completion, documentation, service completion, pilot/tug/mooring readiness and required sailing or outward clearance. Completing cargo work does not by itself imply the vessel can immediately sail.

Final disbursement and invoice reconciliation can occur after departure, including allocation, supporting-document review, queries or disputes. Port-call operational completion and port-cost commercial closure therefore have different timestamps.

P051 chartering memory is refined because NOR, laytime and demurrage replay need vessel-side port-call timestamps and communications, but the agent's event record remains Reality input rather than a self-executing legal conclusion about laytime entitlement.

P014 terminal-handling memory is refined by separating terminal cargo operations from vessel-side agency, navigation-service, authority and husbandry coordination; both layers can independently delay a call.

P039 crew-mobility memory is refined because crew-change feasibility also depends on local agent coordination, transport, authority processing and vessel schedule windows in addition to seafarer documents and border rules.

Atlas known-time discipline is refined because ETA updates, berth prospects, service orders, clearance status, statements of facts and final invoices become known at different times; replay should not backfill final port-call cost or timestamps into pre-arrival decisions.

The atlas already treats ports and terminals as bottlenecks whose congestion changes effective capacity; P052 adds the vessel-side coordination state machine rather than repeating congestion as a macro mechanism.

Earlier crew, security, terminal and inland passes already establish that port calls cross multiple authorities and service systems; P052 only organizes the local agency/husbandry coordination layer among them.

reviewed_no_specific_memory.reason: Agency mandate, authority and liability depend on exact appointment, contract, facts and jurisdiction and require authoritative Evidence.
Tariffs, estimates, invoices and service charges are port-, provider-, vessel- and date-specific facts requiring Evidence.
Provider and authority identities or historical lineages require claim-scoped source collection.
Current port rules, service availability and rankings are time-sensitive source-first claims outside blind Memory.

stop_reason: The vessel-side port-call execution layer is populated from principal/agent role separation and appointment through PDA/funding, pre-arrival information, berth/service coordination, pilot/tug/mooring, authority interfaces, husbandry and survey/service attendance to sailing clearance, event records and final disbursement. Further recall becomes tariff-, appointment-, document-, service-order-, provider-, port- or jurisdiction-specific.
truth_boundary: Memory-only orientation and not legal or financial advice; no agency mandate, port tariff, service order, invoice, pilot/tug/mooring requirement, clearance status, authority rule, survey finding, laytime implication, provider performance or current port condition is verified.
